title: The leaching of phthalates from PVC can be determined with an infinite sink approach
author: Henkel, Hüffer, et al.
materials: The infinite sinks were extracted using Accelerated Solvent Extraction (ASE 200, Thermo Fisher, Waltham, US). The extraction was conducted in two cycles at 120 °C and 40 bar for seven minutes in 11 mL cylinder bodies using n-hexane as a solvent. The solid phase extraction for each sample resulted in ∼30 mL of n-hexane extract, which was transferred in portions of 15 mL into a 20 mL glass vial and concentrated before the refill.

steps.title: Extract infinite sinks by ASE
steps.instruction: Use an Accelerated Solvent Extraction system (ASE 200, Thermo Fisher) to extract the infinite sinks with n‑hexane.

substeps.instruction: Load each infinite‑sink sample into an 11 mL ASE cylinder.
Run two extraction cycles at 120 °C and 40 bar for 7 min per cycle using n‑hexane as solvent.
Collect the ∼30 mL n‑hexane extract and transfer it in two 15 mL portions into a 20 mL glass vial.
Concentrate the transferred extract before refilling the infinite sink (see step 4).

steps.title: Liquid‑liquid extraction of DEHP
steps.instruction: Extract DEHP from the aqueous phase with n‑hexane.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL n‑hexane to the vial containing the aqueous sample.
Vigorously shake the vial by hand for 2 min.
Place the vial in a rack and allow the water and n‑hexane phases to separate.
Transfer the upper n‑hexane layer into a clean 20 mL glass vial.
Repeat the addition of 5 mL n‑hexane, shaking, separation, and transfer two more times (total of three extractions).
Pool all three n‑hexane extracts in the same 20 mL glass vial.

steps.title: Concentrate n‑hexane extracts
steps.instruction: Reduce the pooled n‑hexane extracts to 1 mL.

substeps.instruction: Place the 20 mL vial with the pooled extracts in a laboratory evaporator (Barkey Vapotherm Basic Mobil I, Leopoldshöhe, Germany).
Evaporate under nitrogen flow at 40 °C until the volume reaches 1 mL.

steps.title: Transfer and store extracts
steps.instruction: Move the concentrated extract to measurement vials and store until analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the 1 mL concentrate into 1.5 mL brown glass measurement vials.
Seal the vials and store them at 4 °C until measurement.

description: The experimental procedure provided: the mass of DEHP in the infinite sink (mSINK) and in the aqueous phase (mW) for each sample. For the spiking experiment, the mass balance (mTOT= mSINK + mW) and the recovery of DEHP were calculated. The recovery of DEHP ranged between 85 % and 98 %. For the spiking experiment, the equilibrium of DEHP sorbed to the infinite sink was reached after nine days (Fig. 2A). A decreasing ratio of mW mSINK−1 over time indicated that the infinite sink strongly removed DEHP from the aqueous phase during the spiking experiment and kept the DEHP concentration well below the solubility (Fig. 2B), as desired.Fig. 2Data evaluation of the spiking experiment (error bars indicate the standard deviation, n = 3). Fig. 2A shows the mass of DEHP in the infinite sink (mSINK) in μg at each sampling time. Fig. 2B illustrates the ratio of DEHP mass in the aqueous phase and in the infinite sink (mW mSINK−1) at each sampling time.Fig. 2 For the leaching experiment the ratio mW mSINK−1 likewise decreased as the infinite sink effectively removed DEHP from the aqueous phase (Fig. 3A). It was possible to demonstrate a time-dependent leaching curve of the total amount of DEHP mTOT released from PVC pellets (Fig. 3B). The presented infinite sink method describes a novel approach to investigate the leaching behaviour and release kinetics of phthalates from PVC to the aquatic environment.Fig. 3Data evaluation of the leaching experiment (error bars indicate the standard deviation, n = 3). Fig. 3A illustrates the ratio of DEHP mass in the aqueous phase and in the infinite sink (mW mSINK−1) at each sampling time. Fig. 3B shows the total mass (mTOT) of DEHP leached from the PVC pellets in μg at each sampling time.Fig. 3
